name: BIOSAFETY CABINET
desc: Premium Class II Type A2 Freestanding Biological Safety Cabinet engineered for advanced operator, product, and environmental protection during high-risk microbiological procedures. Features a dual-stage filtration system including a primary HEPA and a high-efficiency ULPA filter.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS BIOSAFETY CABINET is a Class II Type A2 biological safety cabinet engineered to provide simultaneous protection for the operator, the product, and the environment during handling of biosafety level 1, 2, and 3 agents. Its core operating principle relies on a vertical laminar downflow of HEPA/ULPA-filtered air that creates a sterile work zone, while a portion of the air is exhausted through a dedicated HEPA filter to prevent release of contaminants. The cabinet maintains a precise inflow velocity of 110 feet per minute and downflow velocity of 55 feet per minute, ensuring a dynamic air curtain that sweeps airborne particulates and aerosols away from the user. This system is indispensable in clinical diagnostics, pharmaceutical quality control, and academic research, where technicians routinely handle pathogenic bacteria (e.g., Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Salmonella spp.), viruses (e.g., HIV, Hepatitis B), fungal cultures, and mammalian cell lines. It is also used for preparing chemotherapeutic agents, performing PCR setup, and conducting sterility testing per USP <797> and ISO 14644 standards. The dual-stage filtration (99.99% HEPA for 0.3 µm and 99.999% ULPA for 0.1 µm) ensures that even sub-micron viral particles are contained, while the microprocessor-controlled blower automatically compensates for sash position to maintain constant airflow, as validated by NSF/ANSI 49 and EN 12469.
sop: Turn on the main power switch and allow the cabinet to run for at least 5 minutes to purge any residual contaminants.
Check the Magnehelic gauge reading; it should indicate a pressure drop of 13-14 mm Hg. If an alarm sounds, do not proceed and contact maintenance.
Wipe down all interior surfaces (work tray, side walls, back wall) with 70% ethanol or an appropriate disinfectant using a lint-free cloth.
Turn on the UV germicidal lamp using its dedicated switch and set the countdown timer (typically 10-15 minutes) to sterilize the work area. Ensure the sash is fully closed during UV exposure.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value.
After UV sterilization is complete, turn off the UV lamp and wait 5 minutes for ozone dissipation. Then turn on the fluorescent light and blower.
Verify that the downflow and inflow velocities are within specification (55 fpm and 110 fpm respectively) via the digital display or indicator.
Arrange all materials inside the cabinet, placing clean items at the back and contaminated items at the front, without blocking the front and rear air grilles.
Perform all work using slow, deliberate movements to avoid disrupting the laminar air barrier. Minimize opening and closing of the sash during procedures.
After completing work, allow the cabinet to run for 5 minutes to purge any aerosols before removing materials.
Wipe down all interior surfaces again with disinfectant, then turn off the blower and light, and close the sash completely.

Safety Warning: Never use flammable or explosive chemicals inside this biosafety cabinet, as the motor and electrical components are not explosion-proof. Always decontaminate the cabinet with formaldehyde vapor or vaporized hydrogen peroxide before any maintenance or filter replacement.
